questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To be in Europe, to get to a warmer climate, to go to a culturally and historically rich country.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
When finding off-campus accommodation, be careful with using "traditional" renting sites, like idealista - they are pretty sketchy in Italy.
My best tip is to try and check Air-BnB - when booking for several months, the discounts become so large that the prices compete with normal rent, but with much higher quality accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transport (Tram, metro) in Milano is really fast, efficient, and cheap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration was very difficult due to the poorly maintained online page courses. I had trouble getting a learning agreement up until only a few days before, even though I started 3 months prior. I have had to send manual e-mail reminders and complaints several times to even get any answers, responses, and actions in my exchange registrations. The largest problem has been the long waiting times from Milano and the insufficient information that had me applying for courses that were not viable for me anyways.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The only real help was that of my home university - any attempt to contact Milano was met with long waiting times.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The original courses that I had originally planned to attend at Milano was one of the main motivations for applying to the university. A few weeks before going, I was told that these courses were not available for me anyway - a fact that was not made clear from any received information. This was incredibly inconvenient since everything was planned and paid, and I wouldn't be able to stay home and register for classes at my home university instead. The only sensible option was to go; If possible, I would have stayed home, but was robbed of that choice by the incompetent staff in Milano

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you really want to go no matter what courses you wish to attend; Any unforeseen circumstances will be relayed last minute.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: While I attended master courses in Italy, the academic matched that of bachelor courses in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very lecturer-heavy with little to no student involvement and no required reading, compared to my home university.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Structural Bioinformatics: This course offers a practical introduction to biological molecular dynamics in all shapes and sizes; The lecturers are very skilled and the learning outcomes are valuable for anyone in bioinformatics.

questions.answer: Rent in Milano can be very expensive if you choose to find your own accommodations without the help of the University.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Milano has one of the best Erasmus environments in Europe due to its high member count; They are excellent at organising events where you can get to learn new friends.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the initial Erasmus events, and take advantage of the fast and cheap inter-city trains with which you can reach most Italian cities in a few hours. Try to see as many different cities as possible, and find a stable group of friends to travel with.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the fact that Milano has a ton of cafés and bars; Espressos and drinks are pretty cheap. Otherwise I would recommend doing train trips to visit other cities; Milano can get very urban and expensive in the long run.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People in university are very kind to exchange students, and you'll often find that young people are eager to help you train your Italian.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Work up your Italian beforehand.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People seem less motivated at university, which can be tough; A lot of people are late or outright skips class. Italians can be very cynical about other people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Laissez-faire approach to exams; Last minute registration, flexible dates, no strict rules, and trust from the teachers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Start early with your registrations; Write and remind them the moment you think something is taking too long. Italian administration is notoriously unreliable.
2. When you get there, find a group of people you enjoy travelling with and plan as many trips as possible to as many different destinations as possible; For a small-ish country, Italy is incredibly diverse.
3. Try to learn some Italian beforehand, and go there 1-2 weeks before your classes start - social events orchestrated by the Erasmus Student organisation (ESN) usually start mid September; Otherwise it will give you some time to visit some of the more faraway places like Roma or Napoli.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to research whether your area of housing is safe or not before booking; Theft, harassment, and robbery are a lot more commonplace than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a network of friends all over Europe from the Erasmus organisation.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I struggled with a series of unfortunate experiences like getting pickpocketed, sexually harassed, threatened, and assaulted. While I was a bit more unlucky, most exchange students I knew encountered at least one of these incidents while in Milano. Be sure to know which areas of Milano are risky and be careful when alone at night.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
